bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\sin 15^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\), which evaluates to \(0.9659\) — that is \(\cos 15^\circ\). The correct value is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}} = 0.2588\). NOTE this is NOT a transposition of (i) and (ii): the key's entry for (ii) \(\cos 75^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}}\) is CORRECT, since \(\cos 75^\circ = \sin 15^\circ\). Both sub-items have the same correct value, so only (i) is wrong and (ii) must not be "fixed".]

[Textbook misprint: the identity is printed \(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) = \dfrac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\) and is FALSE as printed — the right-hand side shown is \(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\). The correct identity is \(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right) = \dfrac{1 + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\theta}\), which is what is proved above. Checked numerically: at \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{12}\) the true value is \(\tan 60^\circ = 1.732\) while the printed form gives \(0.577 = \tan 30^\circ\). Both forms coincidentally agree at \(\theta = 0\), which is why the slip is easy to miss; sub-item (iii) prints the correct form.]

[Textbook misprint: the denominator's last factor is printed \(\operatorname{cosec}^2 - x\) with no bracket. Read literally the identity fails at every sample angle; it holds as \(\operatorname{cosec}^2(-x)\). Since cosecant is odd and the factor is SQUARED, \(\operatorname{cosec}^2(-x) = \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\) — so the intended factor is simply \(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\) and the stray minus sign is cosmetic, not a sign error in the identity.]

[Textbook misprint: printed as \(4\cos x\cos\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) + \cos^2\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos 3x\), which is FALSE — the second term is a CONSTANT (\(\cos^2 120^\circ = \tfrac14\)), and the statement fails at every one of 7 sample angles. Three corruptions at once: a \(+\) where a product belongs, \(\cos^2\) for \(\cos\), and \(\pi\) for \(x\). The intended identity \(4\cos x\cos\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\cos\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos 3x\) holds at all 7, and is what is proved above.]

[Textbook misprint: the nested-radical identity is printed with NO domain restriction, but it holds only where \(\cos 4x \ge 0\), \(\cos 2x \ge 0\) AND \(\cos x \ge 0\) — all three are genuinely required (it passes at \(x = 0.05, 0.17, 0.31, 0.36\) and fails from \(x = 0.47\); at \(x = 1.21\), \(\cos 4x > 0\) but \(\cos 2x < 0\) and it still fails). The restriction is stated in the solution above.]

[Textbook misprint: the conclusion is incomplete. From \(\sin A = \cos B + \cos C\) the cancellation gives \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \cos\dfrac{B-C}{2}\), hence \(A = |B - C|\), which admits TWO branches — \(A = B - C\) giving \(\angle B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) (the printed answer) and \(A = C - B\) giving \(\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\). The triangle \(A = 30^\circ, B = 60^\circ, C = 90^\circ\) satisfies the hypothesis with \(\angle B\) NOT a right angle. A scan over all triangles found no solutions outside these two families. The printed branch is proved above. The stem also omits the conditional 'if'.]

[Textbook misprint: the stem prints the right-hand side as \(4\cos^2 A\cdot\cos 4A\), but the book's OWN printed solution closes with \(4\cos 2A\cos 4A\), and its derivation \(\dfrac{\sin 8A}{\sin 2A} = \dfrac{2\sin 4A\cos 4A}{\sin 2A}\) forces that form. A superscript-for-argument misprint (\(\cos^2 A\) for \(\cos 2A\)).]

[Textbook misprint, two of them. The stem prints \(\tan x = \dfrac{4}{3}\) while the book's own solution substitutes \(\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2\); since \(\tan\) is negative in the second quadrant, the printed hypothesis is self-inconsistent. Separately, the \(\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\) line prints \(\sqrt{\dfrac{1-\left(-\tfrac35\right)}{2}}\) where \(\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\cos x}{2}}\) requires \(1 + \left(-\tfrac35\right)\); the following step is correct, so it is a one-line sign misprint.]
